## Consequences
- Positive: the T5 replay produces a store whose dates are git's dates and can be validated exactly; `timeline`, `recent` and relative searches evaluated under the same override are consistent with it; the one seam is unit-tested (parse, real-clock fallback) and integration-tested (fixed timestamps at index time, refusal of a malformed value, the daemon's refusal).

## Headings inside markup

CommonMark makes a raw HTML block of a line that is a complete tag on its own (`<Admonition type="note">`, `</TabPanel>`) and runs that block to the next blank line, so a heading glued to a tag without a blank line between (`</Admonition>\n## How it works`, or `<TabPanel …>\n  ### Config`) disappears into the block. The parser scans every HTML block of CommonMark type 6 or 7 (block-level and generic tags) for ATX heading lines (up to three spaces of indent, one to six `#`, then a space or the end of the line) and starts a section at each one. The line is parsed by comrak as a heading of its own, so `# C#` keeps its hash and `# Title ##` drops the closing sequence exactly as outside a block. While scanning, the block's raw content is tracked: lines inside a code fence (opened by three or more backticks or tildes, closed by at least as many of the same character and nothing else), inside `<!-- … -->`, or inside a `<pre>`, `<script>`, `<style>` or `<textarea>` element nested in the block are content, never headings. Blocks of type 1–5 (those elements standing alone, comments, processing instructions, declarations, CDATA) are not scanned at all. This applies to both flavours: a heading glued to `</details>` in a `.md` README is recovered too, which splits a section that used to be one HTML block (one re-summarisation, once).
q: When the parser looks for headings hidden inside raw HTML blocks, which kinds of HTML blocks does it scan, which does it skip, and which regions within a scanned block are never treated as headings?
reference: Only HTML blocks of CommonMark type 6 or 7 (block-level and generic tags) are scanned for ATX heading lines. Blocks of type 1–5 (standalone pre/script/style/textarea elements, comments, processing instructions, declarations, CDATA) are not scanned at all. Lines inside code fences (three or more backticks or tildes, closed by at least as many of the same character) are content, not headings. Lines inside HTML comments or nested pre, script, style or textarea elements are also content, not headings.
required_facts: Only HTML blocks of CommonMark type 6 or 7 (block-level and generic tags) are scanned for ATX heading lines.
Blocks of type 1–5 (standalone pre/script/style/textarea elements, comments, processing instructions, declarations, CDATA) are not scanned at all.
Lines inside code fences (three or more backticks or tildes, closed by at least as many of the same character) are content, not headings.
Lines inside HTML comments or nested pre, script, style or textarea elements are also content, not headings.

## Module contracts

All new code in `crates/mda-core/src/daemon/` except the CLI wiring. Each file has its own tests; the daemon as a whole is tested end to end with the mock backend.

| # | Module | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `store` (additions) | `busy_timeout` 5 s on every connection. `document_hash(rel_path) -> Option<String>` for the unchanged short-circuit. `note_rename(old_rel, new_rel, at)`: copy `created_at`/`created_at_source`/`first_seen_at` from the old row to the new, tombstone the old, emit `EventKind::DocRenamed` with `detail = moved_from`. |
| 2 | `pipeline` (additions) | `index_parsed` returns early when the stored content hash equals the parsed one (line ranges cannot have moved). `sync_path(abs) -> SyncOutcome { Indexed(IndexOutcome) \| Tombstoned \| Ignored }`: index if the file exists and is discoverable, tombstone if it is gone, ignore otherwise. `SummarizeOptions.hot_paths: Vec<String>`: sections in those documents are submitted first, in the given order, then the rest smallest first. |
| 3 | `daemon::watch` | `Watcher::start(root) -> (Watcher, Receiver<Hint>)` over `notify` (recursive). `Hint { path, at }`. `Debouncer::new(quiet: Duration)`, `push(hint)`, `due(now) -> Vec<PathBuf>` releases paths quiet for ≥ `quiet` whose size has not changed since the last hint; `next_deadline()` for the select loop. Pure apart from `metadata()`. |
| 4 | `daemon::hot` | `HotSet`: `touch(rel_path, at)`, `snapshot() -> Vec<String>` most recent first, `expire(older_than)`. |
| 5 | `daemon::ipc` | `Request { Status, Stop, Pause, Resume, Index { path: Option<String> }, Rescan, Watch }`, `Response { Ok, Status(LiveStatus), Error(String), Event(DaemonEvent), Indexed(IndexReport) }`. `socket_name(root)`, `pid_path(root)`, `info_path(root)`; `DaemonInfo { pid, version, started_at, socket }` written to `daemon.json`. `Server::bind(root)`, `Client::connect(root)`, `Client::request(&Request) -> Response`, `Client::subscribe() -> Stream<DaemonEvent>`. JSON lines. |
| 6 | `daemon::mod` | `Daemon::run(root, backend, DaemonConfig, cancel) -> Result<()>`: writes pid/info, binds the socket, starts the watcher *before* the initial `index_root`, then runs three tasks: **indexer** (owns Engine A; applies debounced batches via `sync_path`, detects renames within a batch by content hash, reconciles on structural hints, touches the hot set, wakes the summarizer), **summarizer** (owns Engine B; loops bounded rounds of `summarize_pending` with `hot_paths`, sleeps when nothing is pending, exponential backoff after a round with no success, honours pause), **server** (answers requests, streams events). evidence:
### F2 — "Token economy" saved reads while consuming the user's coding allowance. — **Critical**

**Evidence:** G3 targets "≥ 5× fewer source tokens read per answer." §4.1 says summarization "consumes the user's plan usage"; §4.3 starts concurrency at four workers and adds a reducer call. §11 includes cost per 1K documents and query-level A/B costs.

**Failure mechanism:** Users pay the indexing cost before receiving savings, and pay again when documents change. A corpus queried infrequently—or edited frequently—could never recover that cost. Budgets and AIMD constrain consumption; they do not establish positive value or protect interactive work from competition for allowance. **Gap:** no lifecycle break-even criterion combining backfill, updates, retries, and actual query frequency. Users disable the plugin after it consumes allowance they wanted for coding.
q: In the review of the "token economy" design, what failure mechanism is identified, and what gap is noted in the design's safeguards against it?
reference: Users pay the indexing/summarization cost up front before receiving savings, and pay again when documents change. A corpus queried infrequently or edited frequently might never recover the cost. Budgets and AIMD limit consumption but do not establish positive value or protect interactive work from competition for allowance. The gap is the absence of a lifecycle break-even criterion combining backfill, updates, retries, and actual query frequency. Consequence: users disable the plugin after it consumes allowance they wanted for coding.
